findings.title: SQLite callback can hide a resource-stop exception and permit later slots
findings.trigger: budget.check raises BudgetStop during SQLite execute/fetchall progress callback, before the external hard guard fires.
findings.evidence: CPython 3.12 progress_callback calls the Python handler, clears callback errors and returns a negative interruption code. The SQL caller consequently observes a database error, not the original BudgetStop. The generic replay exception handler converts it to REPLAY_ERROR; backend then reports QUERY_RETURNED. resource_status_in finds no RESOURCE_STOP and the batch may continue.
findings.impact: Violates the registered fail-closed stop-remainder policy and mislabels resource exhaustion as an ordinary replay error. External CPU/wall/RSS guards still apply, so this is not an assertion of unbounded execution.
findings.required_fix: Capture the original callback guard exception in a closure; return a nonzero callback result to interrupt SQLite; execute/fetchall exception handling must re-raise the captured exception before generic replay error conversion. Ensure monitor/probe exceptions also take a fail-closed resource/monitor stop route. Do not rely on exception type-name matching after crossing the SQLite callback boundary.
findings.verification: Static control-flow inspection is sufficient before enablement: every stored guard failure must reach backend RESOURCE_STOP or an explicitly supervisor-recognized monitor stop. Do not run SQL merely to address this review.

findings.title: Fixed twelve-slot denominator is neither retained across early precheck failure nor enforced exactly
findings.trigger: Lock acquisition, registration, execution-gate, original input/runtime integrity, or another precheck fails before validate_inputs initializes report slots; alternatively source_case_indices is changed to another distinct subset of the 21 exposed records.
findings.evidence: Initial batch receipt has registered_denominator=null and slots=[]. Slot materialization occurs only after load_registered(...,0) succeeds. load_registered permits any nonempty distinct valid index list and constructs its Cartesian bounds, instead of enforcing [6,9,14,3] and 12 canonical slots.
findings.impact: An integrity/refusal failure can produce a zero-slot report even though the registered protocol requires all twelve cells, including NOT_RUN. The executable admission also does not enforce the stated fixed source set/order/no-replacement rule.
findings.required_fix: Define the canonical ordered twelve slots for [6,9,14,3] x [2,4,8]; initialize the report with those NOT_RUN slots before fallible lock/prechecks and reject any differing registered source indices/slot identity/order. On precheck failure retain all twelve with the halt reason. Final freeze must bind the exact resulting code and registered protocol.
findings.verification: Read the early-failure paths and literal/JSON registration checks; confirm all twelve rows exist before the first fallible operational precheck, and validate exact source IDs, slot IDs, kind and bound. No target execution required.

optional_P2.title: C-model sanity replay is optional scope expansion
optional_P2.recommendation: A separately labeled C_MODEL_SANITY_ONLY replay can improve dynamic replay coverage if preregistered with full slot cost, but it is not necessary to permit the present limited feasibility trial. A contract model is not the query-SAT counterexample model and must never establish distinguishing-generation yield. If all twelve slots are UNSAT/refused/not-run, report that SAT export and replay dynamic coverage remain unestablished. Do not add a new method just to satisfy this review.

optional_P2.title: Phase costs are not a flat partition
optional_P2.recommendation: Keep process CPU/wall and supervisor wait4 as authoritative. Replay phase costs nest inside the enclosing decode/replay stage; import/connection setup/SQLite close and logging overhead are not all separately itemized. Do not sum both levels. Adding explicit SQLite setup/cleanup/overhead fields would improve attribution, but current enclosing/whole-process measurements avoid a serious missing-total claim.

optional_P2.title: Preparation charge is an explicit reserve, not a measurement
optional_P2.recommendation: The draft's 10 seconds is explicitly labeled conservative and unmeasured. Preserve that disclosure and document its coverage; do not rename it measured CPU or infer precise end-to-end preparation cost. Final registration should reconcile INTERFACE wording requesting an actual prior charge with the chosen defensible reserve/measurement policy.
